Gold farmers, not to be confused with regular "farmers" or "grinders", are players who stay online for extremely long hours and farm mobs for the purpose of selling the in-game money they accumulate for real-world money. The description Chinese gold farmer is often used, as many of these players are Chinese (though recent magazine articles have placed the majority blame on Indonesia). This was strongly suggested when gold selling websites ran out of gold during the , their employees presumably having gone on vacation. Gold farmers then take this money and attempt to sell it to other people through several websites and auctions in exchange for real-world money. This is against the Terms of Se

A gold sink is a game mechanic that helps to control the inflation rate of the in-game economy. Without various gold sinks, the developers would have no viable means of removing excess money from the game's economy. Since coins are added to the in-game economy every time a player kills a monster, completes a quest, or finishes a random dungeon, this would eventually lead to a complete breakdown of the game's economic sub-systems. In a game like World of Warcraft, which is primarily driven by a player-created economy, this could have catastrophic effects. A gold buyer is anyone who buys in-game gold for real currency (€, $, etc.). Sometimes extended to cover someone who buys accounts or virtual assets (items). Some companies effectively buy gold for currency by paying gold farmers for the gold they farm. These actions are a violation of the World of Warcraft Terms of Use and can lead to account suspension and removal of purchased goods/currency.

The Golden Lotus are a mysterious society of pandaren who are guardians of the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. Members of the Golden Lotus are handpicked by the August Celestials to help them keep an eye on the vale, and the pandaren see it as a huge honor to be chosen as a member of the sacred order. The Golden Lotus have recently noticed mogu trespassers sneaking into the Vale and have called upon the Shado-Pan and adventurers from the Horde and Alliance to help solve the mystery of their resurgence. When the Vale was desecrated by the Heart of Y'Shaarj, many members of the Golden Lotus were killed. The rest of the order remained and worked to repair the Vale.

The Gong of Hope is the centerpiece of the great bridge over Forest Heart in central Jade Forest, connecting Dawn's Blossom to the south with the Thunderpaw Refuge and the Tian Monastery to the north. It is apparently looked after by Bellmaster Li. The current bell replaced the original gong, as it was quite small, many centuries ago although the name was kept. The bridge has existed since at least before the Zandalari Troll Wars. It was where Jiang and her cloud serpent Lo first demonstrated the effectiveness of Cloud Serpent Riding in battle.

The Golden Sink was a "reagent" used as a placeholder for the jewelcrafting-crafted panther mounts added in Mists of Pandaria. The humorous name comes from the fact that the mounts would require an obnoxiously large amount of gold to craft or purchase.

The Golden Stair is the grand stairway into the Vale of Eternal Blossoms leading from the Gate of the August Celestials bordering Kun-Lai Summit. The stairs lead into the Emperor's Approach, which continues to the Golden Pagoda to the east and Whitepetal Lake to the west. After the gateway was opened the mogu took the opportunity to invade the vale taking claim to the stairs and building a camp to prevent the doorway from being closed. They guard the area with cannons, constructs, cloud serpents, and even the undead. Golka was the mate of Grommash Hellscream. When ogres raided the Warsong clan, she fought fiercely, taking down several ogres personally. She was mortally wounded during the battle and pleaded with Grom to finish her off. Disgusted at her weakness, Grom called her "a wolf with no teeth" and walked away, leaving her to suffer. Her death brought about the rebirth of the Warsong clan and the beginning of Grom's legend. At an unknown date before she died, Golka became pregnant by Grom and gave birth to a son, Garrosh.

Goldslaves are skeletal trolls that roam the Golden Isle in Vol'dun. They are former members of Pirate-King Zem'lan's crew who attempted to steal some of the Pirate-King's treasure for themselves and were punished by being turned into mindless drones and forced to tend to Zem'lan's treasures for all eternity. First Mate Jamboya, a member of Zem'lan's cursed crew, describes the goldslaves as "de only fate worse than ours".
The Gong of Zem'lan is located at the top of the Golden Isle in Vol'dun. Any member of Pirate-King Zem'lan's crew can ring the gong to challenge the Pirate-King to a fight.

The Goldtusk Gang or simply Goldtusks are a group of Zandalari exiles — consisting of Rhan'ka, Grenja, Man'zul, Volni, and Zulsan — that staff the Goldtusk Inn in Vol'dun. They formerly lived in Zuldazar, where Man'zul was usually the brains behind many of the gang's thefts. In Zuldazar, Grenja got the gang out of a lot of sticky situations by holding open and knocking down a lot of doors as well as people. The group was eventually banished to Vol'dun, but while Zuldazar betrayed and exiled the gang, they never betrayed each other.
